_comment: CANONICAL signature test vectors for POST /internal/email/inbound.
This file is copied byte-identically into the TPS repository at
apps/bff/src/fixtures/inbound-signature-vectors.json, and both test suites iterate it.
The Worker signs with WebCrypto and TPS verifies with node:crypto; they share no code
and never will. A fixed expectation is what stops them drifting, because it is an
ABSOLUTE constant rather than a comparison: change the algorithm, key handling,
encoding or digest on either side and that side's own CI fails, with the other
Generated from TPS's own signInboundRequest - the verifier is the authority here, not
'ascii' also happens to pin hex padding: its digest begins 04, a byte below 0x10, so a
naive toString(16) without padStart produces a 63-character signature and fails here.
'non-ascii' pins UTF-8 on both sides. TextEncoder is UTF-8 and so is node's default
string encoding, but nothing else proves they agree - and a UK construction subject
line reaches an em dash and a pound sign on day one.
